subject: ventures/lawn-aeration-overseeding-bid-calculator
professional: a lawn-care business owner who bids fall core aeration and overseeding for residential lots. First checks: is the seed rate per 1,000 sq ft right for the species and for overseeding (not new seeding), is the aerator production rate realistic for a walk-behind, are both crew members and the drive paid for, and is the target a margin on price or a markup on cost.

evidence.correctness: Recomputed the sample job in an independent Python script (/tmp/claude-0/round94-lawn/indep.py) using the ASABE EP496 effective field capacity C = S x W x Ef / 8.25 ac/h (x 43,560 sq ft) rather than the tool's 5,280 form, and solving the lowest quote by bisection on the margin definition rather than the closed form: capacity 15,840 sq ft/h, aerator hours 1.1995, crew hours 6.1590, labor 151.76, seed 159.60, fertilizer 31.35, machine 25.14, costs 448.49, profit 71.51, margin 13.75%, lowest 30% margin quote 646.10 (68.01 per 1,000 sq ft), break-even 43.04 jobs, profit per crew hour 11.61, take-home 53.63, season 8,582, Job B profit 142.00 and 17.07 per crew hour. node /tmp/claude-0/round94-lawn/tool.mjs prints the same to the cent, and re-quoting at 646.10 gives exactly 30.0000%. The same script shows the markup trap the tool avoids: a 30% markup on cost (562.75) is only a 20.08% margin. Default aerator rate checked against maker specs: 2 ft x 2.5 mph x 5,280 = 26,400 sq ft/h theoretical (Bobcat AE26 rates 40,000 at 3.5 mph on a 26.5 in swath, which the same formula reproduces at ~100%); 60% field efficiency for gated residential lots is conservative and user-editable.
evidence.completeness: README/page features all work end to end in the engine: turf, aerator and seeding hours, labor with burden, seed/fertilizer by lb per 1,000 sq ft, machine and truck cost, card fees, overhead share, true profit, margin, profit per crew hour, lowest quote, price per 1,000 sq ft, minimum-fee check with note, break-even jobs, two-job compare, copy text, CSV, save/load scenario, usage opt-out. Guide worked example equals the engine (page.test.mjs asserts it). Links to the bid-price-engine (trades.mjs has 121 slugs, matching '121 trades', and a lawn-aeration-overseeding row) and three sibling calculators resolve to existing ventures. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs': 21/21 pass before the fix, 24/24 after. Six mutants via quality_mutate.py: lowest-quote denominator without card fees caught; turf = lot (beds ignored) caught; tax set-aside without the max(0, profit) clamp SURVIVED (a losing job then shows take-home above the loss); Job B's miles dropped from JOB_KEYS SURVIVED (compare silently uses Job A's miles); materials-share note threshold 0.4 -> 4 SURVIVED; minFeeApplied > -> >= survived (equal case, benign). Three real-behaviour survivors of six, so 2. Tests added this session kill all three (re-run: caught).
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (201 lines), index.html script, page.test.mjs, calc.test.mjs. Small pure engine, full range validation with readable messages, output escaped, no network, scenario parse validates the main input. Defects: aerator hours modelled as one machine with every crew member paid for the full aerating time (no machine count); parseState does not validate the Job B object (calc.mjs:200), though compare re-validates it; passes accepts non-integers in the engine though the page steps by 1.
evidence.claims: Formula section on the page and the calc.mjs header match the code line by line (checked aerRate, labor, materials, machine, minRevenue). 'Nothing is uploaded' backed by page.test.mjs (no fetch/XHR/beacon/WebSocket) and reading the script. Usage events listed in the footer match the record() calls. Guide numbers are engine output (asserted by test). Disclaimer on page, guide, README, llms.txt and copied text; seed rates are explicitly 'whatever you type; follow the product label and local rules'. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin left in llms.txt, sitemap, robots or canonicals.
evidence.fitness: Walked the job: an owner checking whether a $520 quote on a 12,000 sq ft lot with 2,500 sq ft of beds is worth doing. The tool shows it keeps 13.8% and needs 646.10 (68.01 per 1,000 sq ft) for 30%, and the compare shows the bigger lot fills a fall weekend better. Every input is editable and defaults are visible values, not hidden placeholders. Gaps the owner would hit: a two-person crew running two aerators cannot be modelled (aerator hours are not divided by machines, so labor is overstated on that setup), and there is no per-species seed-rate help.
evidence.domain: Field capacity formula is the ASABE EP496 one; margin is computed on price (cost / (1 - fees - margin)), not markup, which is the right practice and the commonest pricing error in the trade. Seed priced per lb per 1,000 sq ft of turf as extension guidance states rates. Departure: the default 6 lb/1,000 sq ft equals Penn State's full new-seeding rate for turf-type tall fescue (6-8), above overseeding guidance (Missouri IPM and Nebraska turf: tall fescue 3-4 lb overseeding; Kentucky bluegrass about 2), and the page gives no species guidance, so an operator using the default overstates seed cost for bluegrass lawns. Labelled as the user's own number, so held at 3.

defects.what: Three of six seeded mutants with user-visible effect survived: tax set-aside without the max(0, profit) clamp (a losing job would show take-home above the loss), Job B's round-trip miles dropped from the compare (silently uses Job A's), and the seed-and-fertilizer share note threshold. Tests added in this session kill all three.

Aerator hours assume one machine and every crew member is paid for the full aerating time: a two-person crew running two aerators (common on fall routes) cannot be modelled, so labor and crew hours are overstated for that setup.

Default seed rate 6 lb per 1,000 sq ft is the full new-seeding rate for turf-type tall fescue (Penn State 6-8); extension overseeding guidance is 3-4 lb for tall fescue and about 2 lb for Kentucky bluegrass (Missouri IPM, UNL turf). The page gives no species guidance, so the default overstates seed cost on bluegrass lawns. Labelled as the user's own number.
parseState validates the main input but passes the saved Job B object through unchecked; compareJobs re-validates it, so the effect is a late error message, not a wrong number.

verdict: The engine is right: every output of the sample job (aerator hours from the ASABE field-capacity formula, labor, seed, machine, truck, profit, margin, break-even, Job B) recomputes independently to the cent, and the lowest quote is a true margin on price (646.10 re-quotes to exactly 30%), not the markup error common in the trade. Claims and the disclaimer are backed. It misses the bar on verification: three of six seeded mutants with visible effect survived (tax set-aside clamp, Job B miles, materials note); tests that kill them were added this session. A lawn-care owner would next ask for a machine count (two aerators, two people) and species-specific overseeding rates; the 6 lb default is a new-seeding tall fescue rate, above extension overseeding guidance.
